title: Washington Policy Analysts and the Propagation of Political Information
authors: Daniel Bradley; Sinan Gokkaya; Xi Liu; Roni Michaely
eligible_reason: No qualifying specification. The only DiD (Table 2 Panels B-C, and Table 7) uses event windows around brokers gaining or losing a Washington policy analyst (t-3..t+3 around broker-specific years), with control brokers chosen by propensity-score nearest-neighbour matching, a pooled treated dummy (gain_WA_analyst / lose_WA_analyst) and Post main effect in place of broker FE, industry and year dummies, and analyst/broker time-varying controls including the lagged outcome (bratio, pct_xv). Table 3 regresses abnormal commissions on report-publication-day indicators with report-count controls; Tables 4-6 and 8-9 are event-window returns, portfolio and recommendation regressions.
design_notes: SAS proc surveyreg with class year_dummy industry_dummy; WA gain and loss estimated in separate samples. Event-window matched design without unit FE; per the Nov 1 rulings a pooled treated-group dummy does not qualify, and the lagged outcome is an additional violation, so not coded as a near miss.
data_files_note: Table-level analysis datasets shipped; identifiers recoded (Year_Dummy 4-100, industry_Dummy, broker_Dummy are arbitrary codes rather than calendar years/IDs).
data_provenance_note: Values appear original; year, industry and broker identifiers are recoded to arbitrary codes.
screener_notes: Published text read (data/text/mnsc/mnsc.2023.4919.txt; Management Science 70(8), 2024). Regression inventory empty because the SAS file has CRLF/non-UTF8 encoding.
